This appeal is filed by the appellant seeking to grant regular bail, being aggrieved by the order of rejection of bail dated 29.09.2022 in Spl. Case No.55/2022 passed by the Sessions Judge, Special Court at Yadgiri for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n), 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') and under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, (for short 'POCSO Act') and under Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(1)(w)(i and ii), 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short 'the Act').

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the prosecution that, the appellant is the resident of Hosahalli Village.
The victim who is arraigned as CW.7 also belongs to the same village.
It is stated in the charge sheet that, she was studying in High School and she was a minor.
The appellant used to insist her to love him, even though, she repeatedly expressed her unwillingness.
Inspite of warning having been given by the brother of the victim, the appellant did not mend his ways.
That being the fact, the victim also started loving the appellant and it is stated in the complaint that, the appellant had bought the victim a mobile phone and used to talk with her.

3. It is further stated that, on 24.03.2022, the appellant forcibly kidnapped the victim in his Pulsur motorbike and took her to Bengaluru and confined the victim in Alura BDA Apartment, Block No.25, Room No.207 at Makali area, Bengaluru North Taluk and committed sexual intercourse on several occasions.
Thereby, a complaint came to be lodged against the appellant.

4. Heard Sri. Rajesh Doddamani, learned counsel for appellant, Sri. Sharanabasappa M.Patil,
learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and Sri. Chaitanya Kumar C.M, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant that, the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case and he is aged about 20 years, if the appellant is kept in judicial custody, his life would be ruined.
It is further submitted that, the appellant has been arrested and he was remanded to judicial custody on 27.03.2022.

It is further submitted that, though the offences alleged are heinous in nature, the right and personal liberty of the appellant has to be protected, if there is no threat to the victim and other witnesses.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the appellant prays to allow the appeal.

6. Per contra, the learned HCGP vehemently opposed the appeal and submitted that, the appellant is not entitled for any relief as prayed for in the appeal since the alleged offences are heinous in nature.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it appears that, the appellant allegedly said to have committed the offence as stated supra.

However, it is noticed here that, the appellant and the victim are belonging to same village Jagappa @ Jagadish @ Jaggesh S/O ... vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169066252/
2 and community and the appellant is aged about 20 years.
The trial is yet to begin.

Though the offences are non compoundable and heinous in nature, there is no embargo to grant bail to the appellant, if suitable conditions are imposed, the apprehension of the prosecution would be satisfied.
Considering the age of the appellant and the nature of offence, it is appropriate to grant bail to promote amicable settlement/marriage amongst the victim and the appellant, if it is possible.

8. In the light of the observations made above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.

ii) The appellant is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.14/2022 of Yadgiri Women Police Station, Yadgiri pending on the file of learned Sessions Judge, Special Court at Yadgiri in Spl.Case No.55/2022, on executing personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court,
subject to the following conditions:
a) The appellant shall not threaten the victim or any other prosecution witnesses, in any manner.
b) The appellant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court till disposal of the case.
c) The appellant shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In the event of absence of the appellant before the trial Court and if the trial is hampered, the prosecution is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of bail.
